summary.en: Turn ten fruit cards into a table and a plot while keeping measurements separate from answers.
summary.bn: দশটি ফলের কার্ড থেকে টেবিল আর বিন্দুর ছবি বানাও; মাপ ও উত্তর আলাদা রাখো।

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: Carry one row onto squared paper
Make a table that another person can read
Protect the meaning of a row
Read a card in both directions

practice.title: Read one card
practice.statementHtml: State the features and label of p10. Describe where you would draw it.
hints: Read the p10 row before using the axes.
practice.answerHtml: Its features are size six and sweetness nine. The label is mango. Move six right and nine up, then use the mango colour. The identifier p10 is not an axis value.

practice.title: Two records, one location
practice.statementHtml: Draw an apple and mango both at size 4 and sweetness 5. Explain what the overlap means.
hints: Keep both cards even if one dot hides another.
practice.answerHtml: Both dots occupy four right and five up. Two examples still exist. Their labels differ, so these two measurements alone cannot guarantee a unique name for all examples.

practice.title: A student table
practice.statementHtml: Choose two features and one label for predicting whether a student passes before an exam. Explain one column to exclude.
hints: Information arriving after the exam cannot guide a beforehand guess.
practice.answerHtml: Hours studied and attendance are possible available features. Passed or not passed is the label. Exclude final marks because they determine the result after the prediction time and would leak the answer.

practice.title: Repair the notebook
practice.statementHtml: Someone sorted only the size column. Can you safely reconstruct the original fruit records by sorting labels too? Explain a better recovery plan.
hints: Independent sorting does not restore lost pairings.
practice.answerHtml: Sorting labels separately cannot reliably recover which size belonged to which fruit. Return to the original cards or an intact copy, reconstruct each complete record and verify it. Afterwards rearrange whole rows only.

quiz.prompt: Read p6 in the table and plot. Which pair locates it?
options: Size 7 and sweetness 6
Card number 6 and label 7
Size 6 and mango count 5
Size 6 and sweetness 7
quiz.explanation: Its row supplies size six horizontally and sweetness seven vertically. The name mango supplies colour, not a coordinate.

caption.en: Ten fruit cards and their exact two-feature positions.
caption.bn: দশ ফলের কার্ড আর দুই ফিচারের ঠিক অবস্থান।

quiz.prompt: Which two plotted cards share size 3 but have different sweetness?
options: p2 and p3
p1 and p2
p6 and p7
p4 and p5
quiz.explanation: The size column gives three for both p2 and p3. Their sweetness values two and four put one above the other.

caption.en: Ten fruit cards and their exact two-feature positions.
caption.bn: দশ ফলের কার্ড আর দুই ফিচারের ঠিক অবস্থান।

quiz.prompt: On the fruit plot, what does the class colour represent?
options: A third position axis
The known fruit label
The card’s row number
The fruit’s exact weight
quiz.explanation: The legend connects class zero to apple and class one to mango. Weight is absent from this two-feature picture.

caption.en: Ten fruit cards and their exact two-feature positions.
caption.bn: দশ ফলের কার্ড আর দুই ফিচারের ঠিক অবস্থান।

quiz.prompt: If the task is naming a fruit, which item is a feature available before the guess?
options: The hidden correct name
The answer the teacher reveals later
Measured size
A future correction of the guessed name
quiz.explanation: Size can be measured before naming. The true name is the answer being predicted, so it cannot already supply the prediction.

quiz.prompt: What does one row represent in our fruit table?
options: One measurement copied across all fruit
All mangoes combined into one object
Only a list of column headings
One fruit with its observations and name
quiz.explanation: Rows preserve relationships between measurements and the same example. Mixing rows breaks those relationships.

quiz.prompt: Why should size units appear beside the column name?
options: Six centimetres and six millimetres describe different sizes
Units change which label Nana originally supplied
Units make all fruit sizes identical
A table can recover units from row numbers
quiz.explanation: The numeral alone is incomplete. Consistent units let another reader interpret and compare measurements.

quiz.prompt: A sweetness value was never measured. What should the cell communicate?
options: A measured sweetness of zero
That the measurement is missing
The mango label
The previous row’s score without explanation
quiz.explanation: Unknown is different from zero. Keep that distinction so later decisions do not treat invented values as observations.

quiz.prompt: Two fruits share both feature values but have different labels. How do they appear?
options: One record must disappear from the table
Their x positions must differ because names differ
Two records at an overlapping position with different labels
The plot proves one label is necessarily false
quiz.explanation: Equal coordinates overlap. The features may be insufficient, or a label may need investigation; the plot alone cannot settle which.

quiz.prompt: Why is p10 a poor fruit measurement to learn from?
options: It is always another word for sweetness
It supplies a reliable biological dividing value
It guarantees the row will stay tenth tomorrow
It identifies a row rather than describing the fruit
quiz.explanation: Identifiers help discussion but can encode accidental order. A fruit measurement should describe an available clue about the item.

quiz.prompt: For predicting monthly rent, which column is the answer label?
options: Monthly rent
Floor area observed before the guess
Number of rooms observed before the guess
The card identifier
quiz.explanation: Labels depend on the task. When rent is the question, area and rooms can be clues and rent is the answer.

quiz.prompt: What happens if sizes alone are sorted while names stay in place?
options: The original row relationships are guaranteed to remain
Measurements can become attached to the wrong fruit
Only the column heading changes
Every label becomes more reliable
quiz.explanation: Reordering one column breaks the links within rows. Move the complete row when rearranging records.

quiz.prompt: Can a toy table without known group names still support a useful learning task?
options: No, every table must contain an answer column
Yes, because row numbers automatically become true categories
Yes, by looking for similarities without supplied labels
No, numeric observations need labels to exist
quiz.explanation: Features can be collected without answers. Looking for structure is different from predicting a supplied category.

keyPoints.en: One row keeps one example's observations together.
keyPoints.bn: এক সারিতে এক example-এর তথ্য থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A column keeps the meaning and units of one observation.
keyPoints.bn: এক কলামে একই অর্থ ও এককের পর্যবেক্ষণ থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Features are available clues for a prediction.
keyPoints.bn: ফিচার হলো অনুমানের সময় পাওয়া ইঙ্গিত।

keyPoints.en: A label supplies the known answer for the chosen task.
keyPoints.bn: লেবেল হলো বেছে নেওয়া কাজের জানা উত্তর।

keyPoints.en: Two features locate a point on two named axes.
keyPoints.bn: দুটি ফিচার দুটি অক্ষে বিন্দু বসায়।

keyPoints.en: Colours can carry labels without becoming coordinates.
Missing cells and overlapping points need careful interpretation.
keyPoints.bn: ফাঁকা ঘর আর মিলে যাওয়া বিন্দু বুঝে পড়তে হয়।

examQuestions.question: Define example, feature and label using one fruit card.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An example is one fruit record. A feature is an observed clue such as size or sweetness. A label is the known fruit name that this task asks the model to predict.

examQuestions.question: How many examples and measured feature columns are in the ten-fruit table? Do not count identifiers or labels as measured features.
examQuestions.answerHtml: There are ten fruit rows, so ten examples. The two measured features are size and sweetness. The fruit name is the answer and the card identifier is a reference, not another measured feature.

examQuestions.question: Find both size-six cards and compare their plotted positions.
examQuestions.answerHtml: p6 has sweetness seven and p10 has sweetness nine. They share the same horizontal location, six. p10 sits two sweetness units above p6. Both carry mango labels.

examQuestions.question: Design a readable table for six fictional houses whose rent will be predicted.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Keep one house per row. Use clearly named area and room-count features with units, and a separate monthly-rent answer column. Add a reference identifier if needed, mark unknown cells honestly and keep whole rows together when sorting.
